title: Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) Levy Bill 2018
short_title: Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) Levy Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would impose an annual levy on covered domestic commercial vessels to fund national maritime safety services, with charging intended to begin from 1 July 2019.
The Minister would set levy rates through rules after seeking and considering advice from the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) about costs to recover.
Owners and relevant survey certificate holders would be liable, jointly and severally where responsibility was shared, with exemptions available for vessel classes specified by ministerial rules.
changes: Vessels becoming liable partway through a financial year would pay a proportional levy.
The levy would apply to covered vessels in Australia, external territories or overseas.
Costs recovered through individual service fees would be excluded from levy calculations.
Rules setting levy amounts would wait until both Houses had 15 sitting days to consider disallowance.
summary.affected: Owners and relevant survey certificate holders of covered domestic commercial vessels, including responsible partnerships, associations and trustees, and AMSA would be affected.
